title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 286
paragraphs: The river-horse is sacred in the district of Papremis, but for the other Egyptians he is not sacred. This is the appearance he presents: he is four-footed, cloven-hoofed like an ox, flat-nosed, with a mane like a horse and tusks like teeth, with a tail and voice like a horse, and in size as large as the largest ox; and his hide is so exceedingly thick that when it has been dried, shafts of javelins are made of it.
